Thunderstorm winds caused damage in a large area of the Las Vegas Valley.  The AWOS at Henderson Executive Airport measured a gust to 62 mph. The storm also blew over several mobile homes, blew down numerous trees (one of which damaged a car), blew down several power poles and lines, causing power outages for at least 10,000 people, and destroyed at least one fireworks stand.

The same thunderstorm which caused widespread wind damage also caused serious flash flooding. One man who was rescued from a flooded wash suffered minor injuries. Several swift water rescues were needed near the intersection of Warm Springs and Pecos, and at least three feet of water covered the intersection of Warm Springs and Eastern, with several cars abandoned in the water. Several unpaved roads were closed due to flooding in the southeast part of the Mojave National Preserve. Sections of paved roads were covered with debris and grapefruit sized rocks.
Rocks and debris were washed across the Bailey Road off ramp from I-15 North.
Amboy Road was closed near Shadow Mountain Road due to flash flooding.
Water with rocks and debris ran across Highway 62 near Godwin Road.
One foot of water and debris flowed across Goffs Road.  A truck was stuck in the water.
Highway 136 was closed between Highways 395 and 190 due to flash flooding.
Flash flooding caused significant pavement damage to Scotty's Castle Road between the castle and the Death Valley National Park boundary.  The road to Ubehebe Crater was also closed due to flooding.
Highway 95 was closed due to water and debris flowing across the road in multiple places from mile marker 61 to just south of the Nevada state line. A big rig was stalled in one of the flooded areas.
Highway 169 was closed near Whitmore Street due to flash flooding.
Several roads in Sandy Valley were flooded with water and debris.
A four mile section of Highway 266 near Lida Summit was washed out.

Significant flash flooding affected much of the Las Vegas Valley. Numerous roads were closed, and several people were rescued from cars. A church was damaged by three feet of water when a retaining wall collapsed. Several people were rescued from washes. One man died when he fell into the Pittman Wash and was swept downstream.
Up to a foot of water ran down a road in Sloan.

Significant flash flooding affected much of Valley of Fire State Park. Mud and debris flowed over roads in at least ten places in the park. White Dome Road was undercut and washed out. In addition, Exit 75 off Interstate 15 was washed out.
Six to eight inches of water were running across Northshore Road near mile marker 7.
Multiple streets in Boulder City were closed due to water and debris.
The Red Rock Scenic Loop was flooded and closed. One vehicle was nearly swept away.
This gust was estimated by a gas station employee in Kramer Junction.
Highway 62 was closed from Godwin Road to Highway 177 due to flooding in several areas along the highway.
One foot of water flowed over both Bonnie Springs Road and the Spring Mountain Ranch State Park access road just west of Highway 159.

The front windows were broken out of a retail store, injuring one person. Numerous trees and power poles were blown down, and about 30 homes had wind damage to the roofs, mainly in the Plantation Drive area.
Plantation Drive in Mohave Valley was closed by flash flooding. Two homes had flood damage.
Several maintained dirt roads washed out near Old Highway 93.
Highway 95 was closed from Havasu Lake Road to Vidal Junction due to flooding.
Highway 62 was flooded near mile marker 40 with vehicles stuck.
Several large pine trees and power poles were blown down. One house had roof damage, and the Needles Movie Theater had its roof completely blown off.
Water and debris were running across Highway 95 north of I-40.

Flash flooding affected Sunridge Heights Parkway between Seven Hills and Pecos Ridge, as well as Executive Airport Road at Volunteer Blvd. A large amount of mud, rocks and water washed through the parking lot of an apartment complex in Seven Hills.
A 10 foot tall tree was uprooted, and three smaller trees were damaged. Half of a business sign was damaged.
Several roads in the northeast part of Golden Valley, AZ were impassable with at least two feet of water flowing over them.
Diamond Creek Road was flooded north of Peach Springs.
Rocks and dirt washed over Deer Creek Highway, and several secondary roads off of Lee Canyon Road were washed out.
Flash flooding washed mud and debris over Highway 265 near Silver Peak as well as Highway 95 in eastern Esmeralda County.
Three inches of water along with mud and debris flowed down Mesa Blvd.

Major flash flooding affected much of the Las Vegas Valley. Numerous roads were closed due to water, mud, and rocks; and several people had to be rescued from vehicles. Many vehicles in parking lots were submerged in muddy water. Many homes, condos, and businesses flooded, and three dogs drowned in one home. Water got into buildings on the UNLV campus as well as a middle school and the MGM Grand Garden Arena. One landscaper died when flood waters swept him off his front-end loader.

Two feet of water flowed over a section of White Dome Road, and Valley of Fire State Park was evacuated and closed. In addition, Interstate 15 was closed due to flooding of the California Wash (near mile marker 75).
Highway 169 in Overton was closed near the Overton Wash, 1.5 feet of water flowed over Highway 168 in Moapa as well as Warm Spring Loop Road, and there were multiple road closures in Logandale.
This gust was measured on a hand held anemometer.
This hail occurred on Interstate 15, and was produced by the same storm which produced the 75 mph wind gust near Fort Irwin 20 minutes earlier.
Highway 136 was closed, and vehicles were stuck in water, mud and rocks on the road at Swansea.
Lightning struck and injured two Marines on a training exercise.
On Highway 127 north of Baker, one vehicle was stuck in flood waters up to the dashboard.
Lightning knocked out power to 13,000 customers from Bullhead City to Mohave Valley.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 95 in several places just north of Mohave Valley.
Three people in the Las Vegas Valley died of heat complications.
Two more people in the Las Vegas Valley died of heat complications.
A well-known ultrarunner died of heat stroke in Death Valley.
A spotter measured one inch hail.
Several rocks washed onto Katherine Spur Road.
Highway 95 was closed at Five Mile Road due to flooding.
Eight vehicles were stuck at the intersection of Highways 190 and 127 due to flooding.
People in Pahrump, NV observed and photographed a funnel cloud just over the California state line.
A spotter in Charleston View measured one inch hail.
Badwater Road was closed due to flooding.
Part of the Red Rock Scenic Loop was washed out.
The main road to Spring Mountain Ranch State Park flooded near the park entrance.
Several roads in Sandy Valley had mud washed onto them.
Several inches of water and debris were over Highway 159.
Water and debris were crossing Arroyo Road in Blue Diamond.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported by several sources as it tracked from Anthem to East Las Vegas. One car windshield was cracked.

Flash flooding affected much of the Las Vegas Valley. Numerous streets were flooded, and at least one freeway on ramp was closed. Water entered one home, and there were at least four swift water rescues.

Multiple stations measured gusts over 58 mph in the Owens Valley. The peak gust was 79 mph 5 miles NW of Independence.
The California Highway Patrol observed and photographed a landspout near Highway 395 north of Independence. No damage was reported.
This gust occurred 2 miles SE of Mt. Charleston.
This gust occurred 40 miles E of Beatty.
Multiple sites on the east slopes of the Spring Mountains reported high winds. The peak gust occurred 2 miles SE of Mount Charleston at 1150 PST.

Downslope winds affected much of the Owens Valley. A power line was blown down in Olancha, and Highway 395 was closed for a time from Lone Pine to Pearsonville. The peak gust was measured 4 miles NW of Independence at 1242 PST.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at the Las Vegas Ski and Snowboard Resort.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE

events.event_narrative: Eight and a half inches of snow fell at Aspendell.
A skydiver was killed at the Jean Dry Lake Bed when shifting winds caused his parachute to lose lift. At least one media source reported the event as a dust devil, but this is doubtful.
This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake (KBYS).
The peak measured gust occurred 39 miles ENE of Beatty.

events.cz_name: LAKE MEAD/LAKE MOHAVE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA
events.event_narrative: This gust occurred at mid-span on the Hoover Dam Bypass bridge.
A spotter estimated 12 inches of snow one mile north of Goldfield, with some waist-deep drifts due to strong winds.
An estimated six inches of snow fell at Hualapai Mountain Park.
Two and a half inches of snow fell at Morongo Valley.
There were at least six reports of water pipes bursting in Lake Havasu City due to cold temperatures.  Some of the pipes were in attics of homes, resulting in water damage to the homes.
There were at least 50 reports of burst or frozen pipes in Kingman due to the cold.  The entire water system of one hotel froze.
Several pipes burst in Yucca Valley and Joshua Tree due to the cold, including some which caused water damage to buildings. A spotter in Yucca Valley measured a low temperature of 14 degrees.
Several homes in Pahrump had burst pipes due to the cold, and one wellhead also broke. A spotter recorded a low temperature of 11 degrees.
Numerous homes had water pipes burst due to the cold. Several thousand pressure vacuum breakers also broke. Low temperatures on the outskirts of the Las Vegas Valley got down to 17 degrees.
A dust devil blew over two small travel trailers and damaged a solar panel.
The peak gust was measured 4 miles NW of Independence.
Fourteen inches of snow fell at the Las Vegas Ski and Snowboard Resort.
A spotter reported 1.5 inches of snow in Barstow.  The co-op observer also reported measurable snow - the first such occurrence in March since record keeping began in 1981.
Flash flooding washed mud and rocks onto Badwater Road as well as Highway 190 through the Panamints and between Furnace Creek and Cow Creek.
This gust occurred 4 miles N of Mohave Valley.
The peak gust for this event was measured at Bicycle Lake (KBYS) at 0801 PST.
This gust occurred at Twentynine Palms (KNXP).
This gust occurred 5 miles NW of Dyer.
This gust occurred at Mountain Springs.

The peak gust occurred at Bicycle Lake (KBYS) at 0315 PST.  A tree and 12 foot tall ham radio tower were blown down in Barstow, and several trees were knocked down and housing areas were damaged on Fort Irwin.  Multiple roads were closed, including Interstate 40, as dust storm conditions led to several accidents.
The peak gust occurred 3 miles SE of Independence at 1600 PST.

Two mesonet sensors measured gusts to 58 mph.
The Bishop (KBIH) ASOS measured a gust to 59 mph, and a large tree was blown down at the intersection of West Pine and Hammond Streets.
Temperatures reached Excessive Heat Warning criteria for four consecutive days.  One person died and three others were injured.
Temperatures reached Excessive Heat Warning criteria for four consecutive days.  One man died from the heat and five others were injured.
A small brush fire, aided by gusty winds and dry conditions, spread to a home near Decatur and Craig Roads in northwest Las Vegas, destroying the home.

Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. The heat knocked out phone and internet service to Lake Havasu City for several hours on the morning of the 29th.
Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. Three people were overcome by heat in Bullhead City on the 29th.
Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. Two people were overcome by heat in Death Valley on the 28th.

Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. Hundreds of people were overcome by heat in the Las Vegas Valley, including two fatalities. The heat also knocked out power to 132 customers for less than two hours on the afternoon of the 29th.

events.cz_name: LAKE MEAD/LAKE MOHAVE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA
events.event_narrative: Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from June 28th through 30th, and continued into July. Six people were overcome by heat in the Lake Mead National Recreation area, including one fatality.

Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from the 1st through the 4th.  Hundreds of people were overcome by the heat. An unusually high mortality rate persisted until July 11th, by which time 39 people had died (including two in June). Another man died in September after being found unresponsive on July 5th.
Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached each day from the 1st through the 4th.  On the 1st, one person was injured and one dog died from the heat in Oatman.
Thunderstorm winds tore an awning off a mobile home.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a power line.

Thunderstorm winds snapped seven power poles on Route 66 near Oatman, knocking out power to the entire town for 18 hours.  Later in the afternoon, a man was treated for heat-related injuries, and one dog died from the heat.
The general store in Oatman was inundated by flash flooding.
High wind from two dissipating showers blew down trees in North Las Vegas, damaging at least two homes. Several cars were damaged, and some homes lost roof tiles. One fireworks stand also collapsed.
Small rocks washed onto Highway 190 at Townes Pass.
A report of nickel size hail near Anthem Pkwy. and Bicentennial Pkwy. was relayed through Twitter.
Flood water entered two homes in Colorado City.
Six inches of water flowed down Maryland Pkwy. between Cactus and Silverado Ranch, and in the intersection of Eastern and Silverado Ranch.
Several homes were flooded and several roads were closed by flooding in Colorado City.

Highway 165 was washed out just past the town of Nelson, with 14 cars stranded beyond the washout. The debris flow down the canyon was 100 feet wide and six feet deep. A public bathroom structure was filled halfway with mud.

Major flash flooding affected the Carpenter One burn scar. Four feet of water flowed down Harris Springs Canyon, water and debris flowed over and closed Kyle Canyon Road, and mud and debris eventually flowed 20 miles down the mountain onto a few streets in the northwest corner of the Las Vegas Valley.
Temple Bar Road was closed by flooding.
Rocks and debris washed across Pierce Ferry Road, and some side roads were washed out.
Six inches of sand washed across Cane Beds Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew an 18 foot boat off a trailer and into a fence, and also tipped over a box truck. Several areas of town lost power.
Flash flooding closed AZ Hwy. 95 at Willow Drive.
Rocks and debris washed across Blake Ranch Road.
Flash flooding from the Dean Peak burn scar sent a debris flow three feet deep across DW Ranch Road.
DW Ranch Road was closed due to flash flooding from the Dean Peak burn scar.
Thunderstorm winds blew down trees.
Mud and rocks washed across Highway 62 between mile markers 94 and 96.

Thunderstorm outflow winds kicked up a dust storm, reducing visibility to near zero on Pierce Ferry Road between Dolan Springs and Lake Mead City. The visibility contributed to a four-car crash which seriously injured two people.
Several trees were blown down near the intersection of Shaeffer Ave. and Norrie Dr.
A foot of water flowed over Johnson Ave. in Colorado City.

A cluster of severe thunderstorms raked the Las Vegas Valley for over an hour, and also produced widespread flash flooding. Numerous trees were blown down, including 243 at the Desert Pines Golf Course. Some trees fell onto and damaged buildings and vehicles, and some ripped out gas and water lines as they were uprooted. Numerous power lines blew down, and several buildings were damaged. The peak measured gust occurred at Nellis AFB at the onset of the event.

A cluster of thunderstorms dumped rain over the Las Vegas Valley for over an hour, and also produced widespread wind damage. Numerous roads were covered with water and debris, there were at least two swift water rescues, and part of the casino floor of Caesars Palace was flooded.
Flash flooding washed large rocks and debris over Hualapai Mountain Road.
More than eight inches of water, mud and rocks flowed over DW Ranch Road.
A tree blew down and landed on power lines, a tent was torn down, a car was flipped over, siding was torn off the Salvation Army building, and a picnic table was thrown over a car.
Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to near zero in the northern end of the Las Vegas Valley.
At least three trees were blown down, a patio cover was blown off a home, a hanging sign was torn from a traffic light, and 6300 customers lost power.
Two feet of water flowed down Greenway Road near Mission. Two houses were flooded.
One to two feet of water flowed down Harmon Rd. between Sandhill and Boulder Highway. The on-ramp from Flamingo to northbound highway 95 was closed due to flooding.
Sand and small rocks washed onto several roads near Decatur and 215 North, and six inches of water flowed through the intersection of Centennial Pkwy. and 5th Street.
Two trees were blown down by thunderstorm outflow winds. One tree landed on a mobile home.
Power lines were blown down in the Bishop Creek area.
A mud and debris flow trapped vehicles near the intersection of Highway 395 and Haiwee Canyon Road. One vehicle was carried a mile and a half by the flow.
Deep water flowing on Highway 247 south of Barstow caused two cars to get stuck.
Highway 190 was closed at the intersection of Panamint Valley Road due to flash flooding and debris. Debris was also reported on 190 at Townes Pass.
Thunderstorm winds blew down four power poles, knocking out power to all of Fort Irwin.
Debris and rocks washed across Highway 395 at the intersection with Trona Road.
Seven cars were stuck in deep, rushing water on Trona Wildrose Road at Panamint Valley Road.
Eight to 12 inches of water flowed over Highway 58 between Highway 395 and two miles east of Highway 395.
Mud and boulders washed onto Whitney Portal Road and Horseshoe Meadows Road, closing the roads.
Shepherd Creek and Bairs Creek overflowed, flooding the auto tour road and part of the Manzanar National Historic Site.
Rocks washed onto Highway 190 from Furnace Creek north.
Mud washed onto Highway 168 near Gilbert Summit.
Six inches of water flowed through the intersection of Highways 160 and 372 in Pahrump.
Highway 266 washed out at mile marker 6.
Highway 264 washed out at mile marker 8.
Water and large rocks washed over Hualapai Mountain Road.
Four to six inches of water and small rocks washed across streets in Colorado City.
A five foot wall of water rushing down the South Moccasin Wash undercut and damaged Pipe Spring Road.
Several basements flooded in Colorado City.
Highway 168 was closed from Highway 395 across the White Mountains due to flash flooding depositing boulders on the road.
Mud washed over Highway 395 at Haiwee Road, closing the highway.
A funnel cloud was filmed east of the Trona Pinnacles.
Highway 6 was flooded with water and debris.
Highway 375 was flooded and closed just east of the Nye/Lincoln county line.
Moccasin Wash Road was closed due to flash flooding.
Five to 10 inches of water and debris flowed over DW Ranch Road.
Diamond Bar Road was closed due to flooding.

At least three cars were stuck in water, with water lapping over the hoods. Water and debris flowed over several roads, and one swift water rescue took place. Three rain gages in the area measured 2 to 2.5 inches of rain in two hours.
Tree limbs 2-4 inches in diameter were blown down.
A tour bus drove into a flooded wash at mile marker 16 on Pierce Ferry Road, floated down the wash, and lodged on its side on an embankment. Everyone was rescued. The bus was a total loss.
Central Street in Colorado City was closed due to flooding.
Mud and rocks washed across Highway 95.
Mud and rocks washed onto Highway 395.
Mud, rocks and sand washed over Kelso Cima Road at several low water crossings.
Nipton Road was washed out near Ivanpah Road.
Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to about 50 yards in Baker.
St. Thomas Road was completely washed out.

Water up to three feet deep flowed over several streets in Pahrump. Several cars got stuck, and Las Vegas media reported that 20 people were rescued by the Pahrump Fire Department. A spotter measured two inches of rain in an hour and a half.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a 20 foot tall palm tree.
Thunderstorm outflow winds knocked down two trees in Boulder City.
Thunderstorm outflow winds damaged a vehicle by yanking the door out of the owner's hand, bending the hinge.
One man died, with heat as a secondary cause of death (indirect fatality) on a day when the temperature reached 108 degrees.
Five people died of heat-related causes in the Las Vegas area.
One person in Las Vegas died of heat related causes.
One person in the Las Vegas area died of heat related causes.

events.cz_name: LAKE MEAD/LAKE MOHAVE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA
events.event_narrative: One person died in Laughlin of heat related causes during the prolonged heat wave.

Lightning sparked the Carpenter One Wildfire in the Spring Mountains on July 1st. The fire burned a total of 27,881 acres and six structures, and burned well into August before finally being 100% contained.

Widespread flash flooding affected Death Valley National Park. Numerous roads were flooded, covered with mud, closed, and/or completely washed out. Several vehicles were stuck in at least two locations due to flooding.
Gusty winds spread a grass fire to two homes and two vehicles. Two people were injured.
Mud and debris washed over Highway 178 between Randsburg Wash Road and Trona Road.
Large rocks washed onto Highway 190 between Townes Pass and Panamint Valley Road.
Water and debris washed over Highway 190 between mile markers 117 and 124.

Water overtopped a small bridge near the Fletcher View Trailhead just south of Mount Charleston, rendering the bridge impassable. Harris Springs Road was also impassable at mile marker 8 due to flooding. Up to a foot of debris was deposited around picnic tables in the Kyle Canyon picnic area. Ash filled water flowed through several yards in the Rainbow subdivision.
Water flowed over a road near the Jean Airport.
Six to seven inches of water flowed through the intersection of Serene Ave. and Maryland Pkwy.
At least six inches of water flowed across Sunridge Heights Parkway.
Lightning knocked out power to 186 customers in Bullhead City.
Lightning knocked out power to 272 customers in Topock.
Lightning knocked out power to 1002 customers in Mohave Valley.
Mud covered Highway 68 from Union Pass to Golden Valley.
Boulders washed onto the road near the intersection of Alamo Road and Boriana Mine Road. Alamo Road south of Yucca was damaged by flooding.
Six to eight inches of water ran over McCulloch Blvd. in Lake Havasu City.
Six inches of flowing water with rocks and debris covered the intersection of Chino Dr. and Teddy Roosevelt Rd. in Golden Valley.
Several inches of water and mud flowed across the Oatman-Topock Highway at the Sacramento Wash.
Bullhead Parkway was closed due to mud, boulders, and debris in the road.
County Route 1 was closed from Highway 95 to Route 66 due to water, rocks, and debris over the road in low lying areas. One swift water rescue was conducted two miles north of Interstate 40.
Water and mud flowed across the Oatman-Topock Highway at the Sacramento Wash.
A foot of water flowed down Johnson Ave.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 62.
Dust storm conditions along Interstate 40 east of Fort Cady Road contributed to an eight vehicle crash which killed two people and injured five (indirect).
Highway 95 was damaged and closed by flash flooding. One woman died when her vehicle was swept away by the flood.

Interstate 40 was closed at Highway 95, as high water and thick mud stranded several vehicles. A 500 pound propane tank was washed off its foundation. Several stretches of BNSF track totaling about 2.6 miles in length were damaged, and a bridge in the Sacramento Wash was undermined, suspending freight line and Amtrak service.
Mud covered Essex Road, with several cars stuck in the mud.
Water and debris washed over Highway 62 from seven miles east of Twentynine Palms to Shelton Road.
Flash flooding at the National Training Center in Fort Irwin damaged over 160 buildings, with the elementary school suffering the most extensive damage.
Water and mud flowed across Highway 62.
Amboy Road was flooded and impassable.
Highway 127 washed out just north of Powerline Road.
Several inches of water with rocks and debris flowed over Pahrump Road near Sandy Valley.

Very heavy rain on the Carpenter One burn area produced major flash flooding. 18 swift water rescues took place. Numerous roads were closed by flooding, including Kyle Canyon Road (which was washed away) and Highway 95. Water, mud, and firefighting foam covered many streets in northwest Las Vegas for three days as the Kyle Canyon Detention Basin slowly drained. Much of the Las Vegas Paiute Golf Resort was heavily damaged.
Several roads were flooded in the Laughlin area, with one swift water rescue reported.
Two people died in the Las Vegas area of heat related causes.
Two men died of heat stress.
Two people died of heat stress.
Mud and gravel flowed over Stockton Hill Road at Northern Avenue.
Route 66 was closed at mile marker 64 due to flooding.
Over a foot of flowing water with large rocks and debris covered streets in Lake Havasu City. A spotter measured 0.66 inch of rain in 15 minutes.
Water, rocks, and mud flowed over Highway 66 near Oatman.
A car was stuck in a flooded wash on South Estrella Road.
DW Ranch Road was flooded and impassable.
Water and debris flowed across Stockton Hill Road at mile marker 34.
Water and debris flowed across Stockton Hill Road at Red Wing Canyon Road.
Three swift water rescues occurred in Golden Valley.
DW Ranch Road and Blake Ranch Road were closed due to flooding.
Water and mud were rushing down the street at Interstate 40 and Nebo Street. Four power poles were knocked down by flash flooding near National Trails Highway and Minneola Road.
Highway 62 was closed at Sunburst Circle, and a truck and trailer were stranded in swift water.
Morning Star Mine Road washed out in several places with mud and boulders on the road. About seven vehicles were stuck.
Highway 62 was flooded at Mesquite Springs Road. 2.48 inches of rain fell in one hour.
Spikes Road was flooded and closed, and the J Street underpass was also closed due to a foot of flowing water, mud, and rocks.
Highway 95 South was closed near mile marker 71 due to flooding. Water three feet deep damaged Needles Highway, forcing one swift water rescue.
One foot of water flowed over Cima Road just south of Interstate 15.
Water and mud flowed across National Trails Highway near Interstate 40.
Six to 12 inches of water and mud flowed across Highway 247 at Reche Road and also Belfield Blvd. at Encantado Blvd. in Landers. One vehicle was washed away.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 190 between mile markers 121 and 128.
The intersection of Highways 190 and 136 was closed due to flooding.
Water and debris flowed across Highway 190.
Highway 95 was flooded and impassable at mile marker 70.
Highway 190 was closed at Death Valley Junction due to flooding.
Interstate 15 was closed at Mountain Pass due to flooding.
Scotty's Castle Road was washed out, and a car was stuck in flash flooding on Highway 190.
Water entered the basement of a home in Pioche, damaging two bedrooms. Rocks and debris accumulated on several streets. 2.73 inches of rain fell in two hours.
Thunderstorm winds blew a power pole down onto a house.

Heavy rain on the Carpenter One burn area led to major flash flooding. Trout Canyon Road was destroyed, and a nearly completed water line was destroyed as well. Highway 160 was closed near the Tecopa turnoff due to water and mud on the road. The next morning, there was standing water seven feet deep in the highway median, with trees, mud, ash, and debris mixed in.
Water three feet deep flowed across Dean Martin Drive at Cactus Avenue, and the intersection of Cactus and Bermuda was also impassable.
Heavy rain on the Carpenter One burn area led to three feet of water flowing at the intersection of Grand Canyon and Grand Teton.
Six inches of water flowed across Main Street in Panaca. Flooding also caused significant damage to crops on several farms west of Panaca.
Lightning struck and set fire to a house in the Southern Highlands neighborhood.
Two feet of mud covered Highway 266 near Lida Pass.
Highway 159 was closed at Highway 160 due to flooding.
Lightning struck and exploded a transformer.
Water, mud, and small rocks flowed through the parking lot of the Searchlight Nugget casino.

Heavy rain in the Sacramento Wash basin produced high flows in the wash, which covered the Oatman-Topock Highway with mud and water and damaged 50 boat slips at the Topock 66 Spa and Resort on the Colorado River.
A section of DW Ranch Road was washed out after heavy rain fell on the Dean Peak burn area.
DW Ranch Road was washed out between mile markers 3 and 5 after heavy rain fell on the Dean Peak burn area.
A vehicle was stuck in a flooded wash on Stockton Hill Road near mile marker 30.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed at mile marker 17 due to flooding.
A vehicle was stuck in flood waters up to the windows at the intersection of Highway 95 and Goffs Road.
Six to 12 inches of muddy water flowed across Highway 62 at Hendys Road.

Heavy rain on the Carpenter One burn area produced major flash flooding. Several homes in the Rainbow subdivision on Mount Charleston were damaged by flowing water and debris estimated to be five feet deep, and over 30 residents had to be helped from their homes. Highway 157 was closed due to flooding in the Rainbow Canyon area. Highway 160 was closed at Tecopa Road due to flooding. Several inches of water and mud flowed over roads in the area of Grand Teton and Hualapai Way in the northwest corner of the Las Vegas Valley.
Highway 375 was washed out at Lincoln County mile marker 23.
Six to 18 inches of water with mud and debris flowed down Sunset Road from Mountain Vista to Arroyo Grande.
Multiple low water crossings on Cottonwood Cove Road were filled with swift water.
About 9 inches of mud covered the road to Valley of Fire State Park.
Three to six inches of water, mud, and debris covered Highway 62 between Utah Trail and Mesquite Springs Road.
Eight to 12 inches of water flowed across Paxton Road.

Water, mud, and debris crossed Highway 190 between Zabriskie Point and the Furnace Creek Inn, as well as between Saline Valley Road and Panamint Springs. One mile of the road was washed out, and several vehicles were stuck. Mud also washed across Scotty's Castle Road.
Several homes were flooded in the Pioneer Point area. Water, rocks, and mud crossed Trona Road. Trona Wildrose Road was closed near the Trona Airport.
Two to three inches of water, mud, and rocks washed across the 215 Beltway at Ann Road, and also over Cliff Shadows Parkway between Lone Mountain and Alexander.
A foot of water flowed across Beale Street near First Street.
Water and mud flowed over multiple low water crossings on Stockton Hill Road, forcing it to be closed.
Ten to 12 inches of water with rocks and mud flowed down streets in Lake Havasu City. Multiple roads were closed.
A foot of water flowed across the intersection of Kino and Walleck Ranch, and water, rocks, and debris flowed across Sierra Vista between Willow and Bank.
Several dirt roads leading to private property were underwater and impassable. A gage recorded 1.77 inches of rain in one hour.
Lightning damaged two major distribution circuits, knocking out power to about 2000 people.
Water and debris covered the intersection of Highway 322 and Alexander Ave.
Rain on the Carpenter One burn area caused water and debris to flow across roads in the Rainbow Canyon subdivision.
Water and rocks flowed across Calico Basin Road just north of Highway 159.

This gust occurred 3 miles SSW of Mercury.
Strong winds blew down a mesquite tree 3 miles WNW of North Las Vegas.
The peak gust was measured 5 miles NW of Goodsprings at 1134 PST.
Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to one quarter mile along Highways 6 and 395 near and just north of Bishop.
This gust occurred 39 miles ENE of Beatty.
Several trees blew down onto power lines in Keeler. The peak gust was measured 4 miles NW of Independence at 2042 PST.
Strong winds in Twentynine Palms tore half the shingles off the roof of one house and blew down two trees onto another house, causing minor damage.
Strong winds blew paper shingles off some homes and tore down a few small tree branches in Lenwood.

The top of a large Ponderosa pine blew off and fell onto a fence on Mt. Charleston, two Porta-Potties were blown over at Spring Mountain Ranch State Park, and power was knocked out to 72 customers in Goodsprings. The peak gust was measured at the Las Vegas Ski and Snowboard Resort at 0700 PST.
The peak gust was measured 40 miles E of Beatty at 0200 PST.
Power was knocked out to 600 customers in Indian Springs. The peak gust was measured 1 mile N of Indian Springs at 0104 PST.
Several trees were blown down, a large gate was broken, a carport was toppled, and about 1800 customers lost power. The peak gust was measured 16 miles NW of North Las Vegas at 0524 PST.
One man died of heat stroke in the southern end of Death Valley National Park.
Lightning knocked out power to 800 customers.
Flash flooding washed debris over the Willow Beach access road and around the campground and boat launch area.

events.cz_name: EASTERN SIERRA SLOPES OF INYO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A spotter estimated 24 inches of snow in Aspendell.
Several roads were closed in Death Valley National Park due to heavy snow.  Some recreational vehicles got stuck in the snow.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow in far northern Lincoln County stranded approximately 50 cars on Highway 93, with some drivers trapped for 10-12 hours.

Heavy rain in the Las Vegas Valley contributed to 169 vehicle crashes, with 60 injuries (indirect) and one fatality (indirect).  The heavy rain also caused 2000 customers in the Las Vegas Valley to lose power.
The Las Vegas Ski and Snowboard Resort measured 24 inches of snow, and the Mount Charleston Fire Department measured 20 inches. Some tree branches were knocked down and power went out.
The winds were measured at the Bicycle Lake/Fort Irwin ASOS (KBYS).
This gust occurred 5 miles NW of Independence.
The peak gust occurred 1 mile ESE of Red Rock Canyon at 1834 PST.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: A total of 9.9 inches fell in Pioche.

Snow in the Virgin River Gorge led to the closure of Interstate 15 after an accident which was attributed to the heavy snow which fell earlier in the evening. Roughly 300 people were stuck in their cars overnight, and there were 3 injuries (indirect) in the initial accident which led to the closure. A spotter in Colorado City measured 9 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: An estimated six inches of snow fell.
The wind was measured at the Bicycle Lake/Fort Irwin ASOS (KBYS).
Part of a barn roof blew away 3 miles ENE of Joshua Tree.
A few pipes froze in the Las Vegas Valley after several nights of subfreezing temperatures.  The damage was much less than what occurred in a hard freeze eleven months prior.
A few pipes froze and burst in the Kingman area after several nights of hard freezes.  The damage was much less than what occurred with a hard freeze eleven months prior.
Eight inches of snow fell in 6.5 hours.

events.cz_name: EASTERN SIERRA SLOPES OF INYO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Eight inches of snow fell in six hours.
This gust occurred in Bullhead City.
The high winds occurred 5 miles NW of Independence.

Strong winds in the Las Vegas Valley knocked down at least two trees and one set of power lines, and threw a covered horse corral over a fence. About 4000 customers lost power. The peak gust was measured at McCarran Airport.
This gust occurred 3 miles NE of Mount Charleston at 8818 feet.
Two big rigs were blown over on Highway 395 near Little Lake.
These winds occurred 5 miles NW of Independence.
A spotter measured the peak gust near Highway 395 west northwest of Bishop. Blowing dust was also restricting visibility, and was reported as high as 18,000 feet by a pilot.

Heavy rain in the Las Vegas Valley caused a power outage to 1263 customers; shorted out a railroad crossing sensor, causing the gate to block a major thoroughfare; and contributed to at least 43 vehicle crashes, resulting in eight injuries (indirect).
Downslope winds ahead of the oncoming storm system briefly gusted to 60 mph 1 mile ESE of Red Rock Canyon.
These gusts occurred 3 miles NE of Mt. Charleston.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: A sensor near Rachel measured a gust to 55 mph, and a spotter reported minor damage.

events.cz_name: EASTERN SIERRA SLOPES OF INYO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A spotter measured a total of 25 inches of snow at Aspendell. The snow continued into March before ending.
A dust storm reduced visibility to near zero in Twentynine Palms.
Several roads in Yucca Valley were closed due to flooding. The heavy rain also contributed to at least six accidents and three injuries.
Flash flooding covered Randsburg Wash Road just east of Trona Road.
Flash flooding washed out Highway 190. One vehicle was stuck in two feet of debris.
Debris washed onto Dante's View Road.

events.cz_name: EASTERN SIERRA SLOPES OF INYO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: This represents the last four hours of an event which began on February 28th.
These gusts occurred 5 miles NW of Independence.
The peak gust was measured 5 miles NW of Independence.
This gust occurred near Red Rock Canyon.
The peak gust was measured at Bicycle Lake (KBYS) at 1237 PST. There were also multiple brief periods of dust storm conditions.
Strong winds blew out plastic skylights at the Coso Junction rest area along Highway 395.
The peak gust was measured 3 miles NE of Mt. Charleston at 2234 PST on the 29th.
This gust occurred 40 miles E of Beatty.
This gust occurred at Pipe Spring National Monument.
This gust occurred at Bicycle Lake (KBYS).
Strong winds blew the roof off the agriculture checkpoint on I-15 near Yermo.
The peak gust was measured 5 miles NW of Dyer at 1200 PST. Visibility was briefly near zero in blowing dust.
The peak gust was measured 3 miles NE of Mount Charleston at 1234 PST.
The peak gust was measured 5 miles NW of Independence at 1242 PST.
The peak gust was measured at the KBYS (Bicycle Lake) ASOS at 1710 PST.
The peak gust was measured 40 miles E of Beatty at 1315 PST.
A two foot diameter tree was snapped about 40 feet above the ground at Floyd Lamb State Park.
Two big rigs were blown over on Highway 395 near Pearsonville. Dust storm conditions were also reported in the area.
This gust occurred at the Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin.
A fire which started outdoors spread to two houses due to strong winds. No one was injured, but both homes were damaged.
High winds knocked a large tree down onto another tree in the old town area of Mount Charleston.
The high winds occurred at the Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin. The peak gust occurred at 1655 PST.
This gust occurred at the Bicycle Lake (KBYS) ASOS on Fort Irwin.

Widespread damage occurred on Fort Irwin. At least 147 fences were blown down, along with many trees and power lines, and some roofs were damaged. Several power lines were blown down in and around Barstow, and three telephone poles were blown down in Trona. Dust storm conditions contributed to a pileup on I-40 near Newberry Springs involving six big rigs, which caused three injuries (indirect) and closed the interstate for several hours.

A 20-foot tree limb was blown down at Scotty's Castle, eight large metal road signs blew down mainly along Highway 190 on the west side of the park, phone service to Furnace Creek was knocked out, and the power flickered at least 30 times.
High winds blew a large tree onto Joshua Lane in Yucca Valley.
High winds blew over a big rig on Interstate 40 near mile marker 74.
The peak gust occurred 44 miles ENE of Beatty at 1800 PST. Dust storm conditions were also reported by a spotter in Dyer.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: High winds blew down several large tree limbs at Cathedral Gorge State Park. The event time is estimated.
This gust was measured 5 miles NW of Pahrump.
This gust occurred 1 mile ESE of Red Rock Canyon.

Two trampolines became airborne, trees blew down into roads, seriously damaging at least one car, several canopies at Planet Hollywood blew into the street, a carport at an apartment complex tipped over, and about 18,000 customers lost power.
One man died of heat related causes while hiking to Arizona Hot Spring. A woman believed to have accompanied him on the hike is still missing.
Two people died of heat related causes in the Las Vegas Valley.
A tourist died of heat related causes in Death Valley National Park.

events.cz_name: LAKE MEAD/LAKE MOHAVE NATIONAL RECREATION AREA
events.event_narrative: In the Callville Bay area, damage included 17 house trailer skirts; nine trailer awnings; several trailer roofs; flying debris damage to some vehicles, one houseboat, and a dock; a 25 foot sailboat which was flipped off a trailer; and damage to NV Energy infrastructure. At the Las Vegas Boat Harbor, one dock was pushed 20 feet and the bridge leading to it was damaged. Two other docks and private boats were also damaged. One man was presumed drowned in Lake Mead after high winds blew away his boat and caused waves in the lake.
A wildfire in Pahrump burned two sheds, a mobile home, and two motor homes, displacing four families. Two volunteer firefighters also suffered heat exhaustion in the 109 degree temperature.

events.cz_name: LINCOLN COUNTY EXCEPT THE SHEEP RANGE
events.event_narrative: The Cottonwood Fire and Middle Ridge Fire were started by lightning near the Utah state line. The fires destroyed two cabins and a trailer home and damaged a cemetery. Beaver Dam State Park was also closed for a time due to the fires.
The high temperature reached 112F at McCarran Airport in Las Vegas.
One man died of heat stroke in Death Valley. His body was found on the 6th, but he had apparently been dead for three to four days.

Thunderstorm winds sheared four transmission poles south of Griffith Road, knocking out power to all of Golden Valley and parts of Kingman for two hours; and in Chloride, Dolan Springs, Meadview, and White Hills for 16 hours.
A car crash on Highway 68 in heavy rain conditions killed one and injured three (indirect).
Mud washed onto Bullhead Parkway.

Thunderstorm winds in Havasu Heights destroyed one home, moved one mobile home off its foundation, damaged several garage doors, damaged several roofs, blew out numerous home and vehicle windows, overturned RVs, and blew away one chicken coop and several chickens.
Thunderstorm winds blew down 44 power lines near Sara Park, knocking out power to southern portions of Lake Havasu City.
Route 66 near Topock was closed due to flooding.
Six to eight inches of water flowed over Valley Park Way at Puma Road.
Water was up to car doors in downtown Kingman.
Water one to two feet deep flowed over Diamond Creek Road.
A rockslide occurred along Interstate 40 between mile markers 47 and 48. The interstate itself was not affected.
Water at least a foot deep flowed down the streets in Topock.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a mesquite tree.
Thunderstorm winds damaged the roof of a closed restaurant.
Flash flooding closed Highway 1 north of Topock.
Many roads in Twentynine Palms were flooded, and several drivers had to be rescued. A spotter measured 1.92 inches of rain in two hours.
Thunderstorm winds blew down at least 14 power poles in Twentynine Palms, knocking out power to 2,000 customers.
Highway 95 was closed between Interstate 40 and Highway 62 due to flooding in multiple places. There was at least one swift water rescue.
Roads in and around Baker, including Kelbaker Road and Highway 127, were closed due to flooding. Several vehicles were stuck.
Parts of Highway 178 were closed near Shoshone due to flooding.
Dante's View Road was closed due to flooding.
Thunderstorm winds blew down 6-8 inch tree branches.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 95.
Several trucks were stuck in about a foot of flowing water near A Street and Main Street.
The intersection of Highways 95 and 62 was flooded with lots of debris.
Thunderstorm winds blew down two 12-foot tall trees.
Flash flooding closed several roads in, north, and south of Needles.
A car was stuck in flash flooding at the intersection of Del Rey Drive and Pahaska Trail.
Multiple vehicles were stuck in flowing water two to three feet deep on Highway 95.
Outflow winds from distant thunderstorms beached two boats, including one house boat.
A swift water rescue was performed at the intersection of Decatur and Oakey when a car drove into deep water in the intersection.
Highway 95 was flooded and impassable near Beatty.
Flash flooding knocked the gate to the Griffith Peak trailhead off its hinges and blocked Harris Springs Road with debris.
Four to six inches of water and mud flowed across a side road.
Parts of Needles Highway washed out just north of the NV/CA border.
This gust occurred at the Kane Springs RAWS.
Three stations recorded gusts of 58 to 60 mph.
Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to near zero in Pahrump.
Water, mud, and rocks flowed over Kyle Canyon Road.
This gust occurred at Sierra Vista High School.
Six to 12 inches of water flowed over Durango Drive at and north of Blue Diamond Road. The Blue Diamond Channel ALERT recorded 1.10 inches of rain in 30 minutes.
This gust occurred 5 miles SW of Jean.
Thunderstorm winds over Lake Mead triggered swells up to eight feet that sank at least one vessel. 11 people had to be rescued.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
One woman died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
Several roads were flooded and impassable in Meadview.
A fruit stand was destroyed and a window was blown out of a business.
Temple Bar Access Road was flooded between mile markers 22 and 23.
Water 12-18 inches deep flowed over Pierce Ferry Road at Archibald Wash.
At least six inches of flowing water and rocks crossed Willows Ranch Road at Willow Creek.
Excessive Heat Warning criteria were reached in Las Vegas as the high temperature reached 112F.
Dust storm conditions reduced visibility to less than a quarter mile in Kingman.
Flash flooding in Kingman left numerous roads impassable on the north side of town, caused minor damage to 20 homes, and necessitated six swift water rescues.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large trees and at least 10 power poles and power lines, and blew the roof off a shed.
Hail up to nickel size fell with the same storm which produced the damaging winds and flash flooding.
This gust was measured at the Kane Springs RAWS.
Lightning struck and set fire to two palm trees.
Water up to six inches deep flowed through the Rainbow Canyon subdivision.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
Las Vegas reached Excessive Heat Warning criteria with a high temperature of 112F.
Water over six inches deep flowed down streets near downtown Kingman, and a rockslide closed Andy Devine Avenue near Chadwick Drive.

A dust storm brought visibility down to one quarter mile or less in Kingman, Dolan Springs, and Chloride. A vehicle rolled over on Highway 93, during the dust storm, resulting in four injuries (indirect).
The Willow Beach access road was closed due to flash flooding which washed gravel onto the road.
Water and rocks flowed over Highway 62.
Pieces of pavement washed off Interstate 15 at the Halloran Summit Road exit.
Water and mud covered Nipton Road.
Flash flooding covered several lanes of Interstate 15 near Jean, forcing traffic into the median. Highway 161 from Jean to Goodsprings was closed, and rocks and mud also washed onto secondary roads.
Lightning set fire to a tree.

Major flash flooding occurred downstream of the Carpenter One burn area. Water and debris five feet deep came down Rainbow Canyon. Six homes were damaged, including two with major damage. Rainbow Canyon Road was damaged, as were utility lines and a water pipe.
Lightning set fire to a palm tree.
Highway 322 was closed due to flooding from mile marker 5 to the Rose Valley turnoff. A portion of the road was washed out.
Thunderstorm winds knocked trees onto power lines.
Eight to ten inches of flowing water, mud, and rocks washed across low spots on several roads.
Water flowed across the intersection of Bank and Armour Streets, and water and small rocks also flowed across Hualapai Mountain Road.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a dozen power poles and took down at least 50 power lines, removed shingles from roofs, ans bent a garage door. 14,200 people lost power.
Lightning struck and damaged a house.
Water and large rocks flowed across Stockton Hill Road near mile marker 8.
Water up to six inches deep flowed down several streets in Lake Havasu City.
Three cars ended up in the wash off Estrella Road, and a total of 13 people were rescued from vehicles around town. At least three people had to wait on top of their cars.
Six inches of water flowed over Bank St. between Airway Ave. and Northern Ave. There was also flooding on Irving St. between Kino Ave. and Gordon Dr.
Water and debris were over the Willow Beach access road.
Temple Bar Access Road was impassable due to flooding from the Detrital Wash.
Kingman Wash Access Road was washed out.
Dust storm conditions on Interstate 40 near Newberry Springs led to a series of accidents involving seven big rigs and three cars. Nine people were injured (indirect).
Several inches of water and mud flowed over roads in the Manzanar National Historic Site, closing the auto tour road.
Rocks and debris washed onto sections of Whitney Portal Road from west of Lone Pine all the way to the parking area for the trail.
Flash flooding along Highway 62 closed the highway, trapping about 400 cars between flooded washed. One swift water rescue occurred.
Highway 95 flooded in multiple places between Needles and Vidal Junction.
Cedar Canyon Road was blocked by a large flow of mud and rocks.
Water and mud washed over National Trails Highway near Amboy.

One to two feet of water flowed through streets in southwest Barstow. At least five swift water rescues took place, three homes were flooded with water and mud, and a 20-inch sewer line was ruptured. Lenwood Road was washed out in sections between National Trails Highway and the I-15 on ramp, with one vehicle stuck. The intersection of Calico Blvd. and Ghost Town Road was also flooded with a vehicle stuck. Minneola Road was closed from Mitchells Ranch to Valley Center. A two-vehicle crash occurred during the heavy rain, injuring two people (indirect).
The intersection of Highways 58 and 395 was fully flooded.
Rocks and debris flowed over National Trails Highway at Ludlow Road.
Highway 395 was flooded near San Bernardino County mile marker 32.

A foot of water and debris flowed over Highway 190 at State Line Road just outside Death Valley National Park. The water also burst into the historic Amargosa Opera House, warping the original wood floors in the 91 year old building.
Ubehebe Crater Road was closed at the junction with Scotty's Castle Road due to flood damage.
Highway 165 was closed due to water and debris.
Debris washed over Lakeshore Road.
Several roads in Moapa were flooded and covered with mud.
Harris Springs Road and some secondary roads in lower Kyle Canyon were washed out.
Highway 159 was closed by flooding and debris. Spring Mountain Ranch State Park was also closed.
A small tornado briefly touched down in open desert east of Highway 95 near the Nelsons Landing turn off.
Highway 95 was flooded near the intersection of Highway 160 as well as near Nye County mile markers 18 and 20.
Several inches of water and debris flooded roads on Area 6 of the Nevada National Security Site.

Water was several inches deep at the intersection of Twain and Decatur. A swift water rescue occurred at Decatur and Oakey. A large section of concrete block wall was knocked down by floodwaters. A car stalled in the water at Rainbow and Hacienda. Water was several inches deep over the intersection of Koval and Winnick. 143 weather related accidents were reported.
Arroyo Road was flooded 8-12 inches deep.
Two lanes of Highway 95 were flooded with several inches of water.
Part of Highway 157 was washed out. Highway 95 was closed at Clark County mile marker 99, with 30 cars stranded and some washed off the road. Everyone was rescued.
Highway 93 was flooded and closed at Lincoln County mile marker 3.
Over a foot of water flowed rapidly down Grand Teton Drive.
Highway 95 was damaged by flooding near Nye County mile marker 75.
Mud and debris washed onto Highway 265.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
One man died in Las Vegas of heat related causes.
Water, rocks, and mud flowed over several roads in Oatman. Waterfalls formed in the Black Mountains.
The Willow Beach access road was damaged and closed due to flooding.
Water covered Route 66 south of Golden Shores, and the road was eventually closed all the way south to I-40.
Nipton Road was washed out, and a big rig was stuck in the wash.

Thunderstorm winds blew the roofs off two restaurants, damaged several roofs of homes, blew down some signs and at least 50 power poles, and blew down several trees in and around Needles. One person was injured when a roof collapsed.
A series of thunderstorms caused street flooding in Needles. The first storm in the series caused the wind damage documented in a separate entry.
Highway 95 was closed from 5 Mile Road to Interstate 40 due to flood damage. One swift water rescue occurred at mile marker 56.
Goffs Road and Highway 95 were both impassable due to flooding.
Water and rocks flowed swiftly across Highway 95 between mile markers 70 and 71.
Highway 62 was flooded near the Highway 95 intersection.
Lightning caused a tree fire and also struck a power pole, causing a power outage which, along with the rain, contributed to a multi-vehicle accident which injured one person (indirect).
Over six inches of water flowed over Lakeshore Road north of the Lake Mead National Recreation Area entrance, forcing the road to be closed.
Thunderstorm winds damaged floating docks at the Las Vegas Boat Harbor.
Rocks and mud flowed down Isabel Street at Robinson Lane.
The Oatman-Topock Highway was closed from mile markers 1 to 7 due to flooding.
Many streets in central Kingman were closed due to flooding.
Two to two and a half feet of water flowed over Pierce Ferry Road at Archibald Wash.

Several trees were blown down in Bullhead City, including some onto cars and one onto a mobile home. Two power poles were broken and several power lines taken down, knocking out power to about 6000 customers. One roof was blown off, and some other buildings had minor roof damage. A light pole was knocked down, and a satellite dish was bent. The KIFP ASOS recorded a peak gust of 68 mph.
Eight inches of water flowed over the intersection of Laguna and Jupiter.
Water and debris flowed over the road to Katherines Landing.
Gravel and rocks washed across Stockton Hill Road at mile marker 10.
Eight to ten inches of water flowed over Bacobi Road just south of Highway 68.
A vehicle was stuck in several feet of water where the Sacramento Wash crosses the Oatman-Topock Highway.
Rocks and debris washed over many of the side roads in Colorado City, and also over low lying spots on Cane Beds Road.
White Hills Road was washed out in multiple places.
Stockton Hill Road was closed from mile marker 16 to mile marker 40, and Pierce Ferry Road was closed at mile marker 16 due to flooding.

The KDAG ASOS reported a gust to 60 mph. Sixteen power poles were blown down along Newberry Springs Road, forcing the road to be closed. Trees were blown down and a garage door was damaged in Newberry Springs.
A spotter measured 1.72 inches of rain, and reported that all road within about three square miles were closed due to flooding.
Water six to seven inches deep flowed over Highway 127.
Highway 95 was closed from Goffs Road to about 12 miles south of the Nevada state line due to flooding. Twelve vehicles were stranded between two washouts.
Thunderstorm winds blew a tree onto a vehicle at a rest area on Interstate 40.
Several accidents occurred along Interstate 15 near Nipton Road due to heavy rain, including one rollover and one jack knifed big rig. One person was injured (indirect).
Essex Road was flooded near Interstate 40.
Rocks and debris washed over Nipton Road near Interstate 15.
Rocks washed across National Trails Highway near Danby Road.
Six to eight inches of water flowed over Morning Star Mine Road between mile markers 1 and 3.
Cima Road was flooded near Interstate 15.
Mud and debris washed over Highway 62 near Utah Trail, and the edges of the pavement were washed out.
Moapa Valley Blvd. was flooded just south of the Simplot plant.
Gravel and debris washed over Northshore Road, and the road to St. Thomas was also closed.
The California Wash flooded and closed Hidden Valley Road.
The Pahranagat Wash flooded and closed Warm Springs Road.
Six Mile Cove Road was impassable due to flooding.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Cal-Nev-Ari.
Several roads were impassable in Cal-Nev-Ari. A spotter measured 2.10 inches of rain.
Needles Highway was closed from Casino Drive to the California state line.

Swift water flowed across Patti Ann Woods Drive just west of College Drive, mud and rocks from a vacant lot washed onto Horizon Ridge Parkway near Nautical Street, and baseball sized rocks washed onto Horizon Drive at Horizon Ridge Parkway.
Valley of Fire Highway was flooded just south of Interstate 15.
A spotter driving on Highway 93 southeast of Wikieup estimated a 65 mph gust from a thunderstorm. He had to pull over and stop because his car was being blown off the road.
A spotter measured three quarter inch hail.
Two feet of water flowed over Hualapai Mountain Road between mile markers 5 and 6.
Stockton Hill Road was flooded between mile markers 22 and 34 with a few cars stuck in the water. The road was closed for several hours due to an eight foot deep rut carved  in the road.
A spotter estimated nickel size hail at Diamond M Ranch.
Temple Bar Access Road was washed out from mile marker 26 onward.
Two feet of water flowed over Pierce Ferry Road at Archibald Wash.
Over six inches of water flowed down Main Street in Oatman.
Over a foot of muddy water flowed over the Oatman-Topock Highway at the Sacramento Wash.
Major flash flooding impacted the Virgin River Gorge. Interstate 15 was closed for several hours due to water and debris over the highway. Many waterfalls flowed off the higher terrain.
Cars were stuck near the intersection of AZ Highway 95 and Acoma Blvd., with a swift water rescue occurring.
Up to six inches of water flowed over low spots on Newberry Road, including the intersection with Route 66.
Kelso Cima Road was flooded near Kelso Depot.
Mud and debris up to a foot deep covered a 200 foot long stretch of road near the intersection of National Trails Highway and Danby Road.
Water and rocks flowed over the intersection of National Trails Highway and Amboy Road.
Highway 62 was closed due to flooding.
Lots of large rocks and debris were over the Nipton Road off ramp from Interstate 15, and flood waters also crossed Nipton Road near Ivanpah Road.
A bridge was washed out on Route 66 southwest of Essex, and mud was over the roads in and around Essex.
Interstate 40 was flooded.
A large chunk of Highway 95 just south of Needles was washed away.
Amboy Road was flooded at Midway Road with lots of debris on the road. Water was still running hours later.
Highway 127 was flooded and closed, with two cars stuck in the water.
Highway 95 washed out at Goffs Road.
Three feet of water crossed National Trails Highway at Essex.
Highway 95 was flooded at mile marker 10. Some vehicles were stuck and others were swept into the desert.
Four feet of water flowed over Highway 95 with cars stuck in the water.
Over a foot of water flowed over Trails End Road and A Street.
Hail up to nickel size was estimated at Charleston and 215.
One vehicle was stuck in six to 12 inches of standing water on the Flamingo Road off ramp from I-215.
Lots of mud and rocks washed onto Tropicana between Hualapai and Fort Apache.
Numerous roads were impassable in the Moapa River Indian Reservation area due to flooding on the Muddy River.
Corn Creek Road was washed out.
Deer Creek Road was washed out between mile markers 2 and 4.
Highway 168 was closed from Coyote Springs to Moapa due to flooding.
Several swift water rescues took place near and west of Fort Apache and Russell. At least six inches of water, mud, and rocks flowed over Tropicana and Grand Canyon.

Major flash flooding affected the Moapa, Logandale, and Mesquite areas. Several local roads were washed out and some were covered with five feet of silt. At least 20 homes were damaged and many people were evacuated. Parts of the Union Pacific railroad track were washed out. The parking lot of a power generating plant was filled with six feet of flood water. Interstate 15 suffered major damage and was closed for days. Cars floated down the highway, and one person was injured when he jumped in to help the occupants of a minivan which was swept over a 10-15 foot drop. Four earthen dams were breached in the area.
Cars were stuck in water and mud on Columbia Pass outside Sandy Valley. More than half of the dirt roads in Sandy Valley were damaged.
Rapidly flowing water flooded the parking garage of the Quad Resort on the Las Vegas Strip. One construction worker was swept away but was not injured.
Arroyo Road was closed due to flooding.
The Muddy River flooded Moapa, Logandale, and Overton. A total of 139 homes and the Cooper Street Bridge were damaged.
Mud and debris covered Highway 322 just east of Pioche, and there was erosion damage to several agricultural fields in the area.
A mud slide washed out a section of Union Pacific railroad track, derailing a locomotive.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to Interstate 40 due to flooding.
London Bridge Road was impassable due to flooding from a rapidly flowing wash.
Trained spotter reported one inch hail 4 miles northeast of Dolan Springs.
Antares Road was flooded and closed at the Truxton Wash.
Stockton Hill Road was closed from Pierce Ferry Road to Vock Wash.
Seventh Street was impassable due to a flooded wash. A fire truck was stranded overnight.

Severe flooding impacted much of Joshua Tree. Many roads were covered with water, mud, and rocks. Several homes were flooded, including one which was destroyed. A one year old boy was swept away in his back yard before being rescued. One man died when his vehicle was swept down a flooded wash.
Trained spotter reported one inch hail 2 miles south of Joshua Tree.
Highway 95 was closed from Five Mile Road to Highway 62 due to flooding in several places. Five feet of water, mud, and debris flowed over the highway just north of Vidal Junction.
Park Service reported one inch hail at Pipe Spring National Monument.
Twenty Mule Team Road, Salt Creek Road, and Titus Canyon Road were all damaged by flash flooding.
Thunderstorm winds blew a tree onto Sunland Lane, blocking half of the road. The Bishop ASOS recorded a peak gust of 56 mph several minutes before the tree fell.
The Oatman-Topock Highway was closed due to flooding at the Sacramento Wash. The first evidence of flooding was a webcam picture at 6 AM, but the actual start time is unknown.
Lightning struck and damaged Southern California Edison equipment, knocking out power to 15 customers.
Lightning struck and set fire to two power poles along Highway 95 at Nye County mile marker 79. Rain extinguished the fire.
Lightning struck and set fire to the abandoned historic Rhyolite Mercantile Building, destroying it.
Boulders up to softball sized washed onto Highway 190 at mile marker 66.
Several inches of water and debris flowed over Highway 66.
DW Ranch Road was flooded between mile markers 3 and 4.5.
Six inches of water flowed over Estrella Road at 0545 MST. Two swift water rescues occurred at 0800 MST.
Pierce Ferry Road was closed from mile marker 10 to Diamond Bar Road due to flooding. The road was washed out near Meadview.
Colorado City Fire Department reports quarter sized hail in town.
Stockton Hill Road was closed briefly due to flooding and debris on the road.
Numerous roads were flooded in Colorado City, including every Short Creek crossing in town.
This event occurred 40 miles E of Beatty.
Warm Springs Road was flooded and impassable. The spotter measured 1.67 inches of rain, most of which fell in 45 minutes.
This gust occurred 40 miles E of Beatty.
Water and large rocks were flowing across Highway 93 six miles south of Coyote Springs, and water was also starting to come over the road half a mile north of Coyote Springs.
Six to eight inches of water flowed over several roads in Boulder City.
This gust occurred at the North Las Vegas airport.
Lightning struck and set fire to a palm tree in the 7300 block of Raincloud Drive.
Thunderstorm winds blew a heavy construction barricade into a car, causing significant damage.
Several drivers were stranded in water 1-2 feet deep at Rancho and Alexander.
Lightning struck and set fire to a townhouse.
Public reported 3/4 hail at Charleston and Fort Apache.
Highway 93 was flooded between Lincoln County mile markers 65 and 70.
Thunderstorm winds broke off numerous small tree limbs, blew in the door of a business, and uprooted a large tree.
The intersection of Decatur Rd. and Horse Dr. was impassable due to flooding.
Flooding on the Muddy River closed Highway 168 5 miles NW of Moapa.

Lake Havasu City saw its first ever recorded accumulating snow, with up to two inches on the east side. Snow fell all the way down to the river, but did not accumulate there.
Three inches fell at both Pipe Spring National Monument and Colorado City. Several vehicles slid off roads and/or into other vehicles due to snowy roads. The event continued into January 2015.
